boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on campus-adjacent Princeton corridors, each with a documented reason to stop.

cards.title: See a free gallery in Bainbridge House
cards.subtitle: Nassau Street corridor · 158 Nassau St.
cards.notes: Walk Nassau Street to the restored Bainbridge House and check the current Art Museum exhibition before heading inside.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art gallery in a preserved 1766 house.
cards.evidence_claim: Art@Bainbridge is a Princeton University Art Museum gallery project at 158 Nassau Street, with free admission.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current exhibition details before visiting.

cards.title: Catch an art-house film
cards.subtitle: Nassau Street corridor · 160 Nassau St.
cards.notes: Use the theatre’s program to choose an independent, foreign, or classic film, then plan parking or the town shuttle.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit community art-house cinema on Nassau Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The nonprofit Garden Theatre at 160 Nassau Street presents independent, foreign, and classic films.
cards.access_notes: Ticket purchase may be required; check the current film schedule.

cards.title: Browse an event or the stacks
cards.subtitle: Witherspoon Street corridor · 65 Witherspoon St.
cards.notes: Check the library calendar for author talks, classes, exhibitions, or films, then visit during its posted public hours.
cards.short_summary: A public library with a broad calendar of talks, classes, and exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton Public Library at 65 Witherspoon Street publishes events including author talks, classes, exhibitions, and films.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Mon–Thu 9 a.m.–8 p.m.; Fri–Sat 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; Sun noon–5 p.m.

cards.entity_name: Paul Robeson Center for the Arts
cards.title: Visit a working arts center
cards.subtitle: Witherspoon Street corridor · 102 Witherspoon St.
cards.notes: Look for current gallery exhibitions or public programs at the Arts Council, at the corner of Witherspoon and Paul Robeson Place.
cards.short_summary: The Arts Council’s gallery, theater, studio, and meeting-space home.
cards.evidence_claim: The Paul Robeson Center for the Arts at 102 Witherspoon Street includes a gallery, theater, studios, and public meeting space.
cards.source_title: Our History | Arts Council of Princeton
cards.access_notes: Gallery and building hours are posted by the Arts Council; some classes and events may require registration or tickets.

cards.title: Walk historic garden grounds
cards.subtitle: Stockton Street corridor · 55 Stockton St.
cards.notes: Take the Stockton Street approach and allow time for the garden; the museum’s visitor page lists separate garden and museum access details.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark with museum exhibitions and gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Morven at 55 Stockton Street is a public museum and garden; its garden is open daily from dawn until dusk.
cards.access_notes: Museum hours are Wednesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; garden hours are dawn to dusk. Check admission details before entering the museum.

cards.title: Start with the Dinky terminal
cards.subtitle: Alexander Street corridor · 152 Alexander St.
cards.notes: Use the station as a transit waypoint: the Dinky connects Princeton Station and Princeton Junction, with local bus links nearby.
cards.short_summary: The Princeton end of NJ Transit’s short Dinky rail connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton Station is at 152 Alexander Street, and the Dinky connects it with Princeton Junction.
cards.source_title: Getting Around Princeton | Municipality of Princeton
cards.access_notes: Check NJ Transit service information and fares before travel.

cards.title: Follow battlefield interpretive trails
cards.subtitle: Mercer Road corridor · park access from Mercer Rd.
cards.notes: Reach the park by the paved Mercer Road path, then follow the perimeter trails and interpretive signs around the historic field.
cards.short_summary: A Revolutionary War landscape with trails, signage, and landmark sites.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton Battlefield State Park has paved and natural trails, interpretive signage, the Clarke House, and battlefield landmarks.
cards.source_title: Princeton Battlefield State Park | Municipality of Princeton
cards.access_notes: The municipality states the park is reachable on foot or by bike via the paved Mercer Road path; stay on maintained public trails.

cards.title: Use the courtyard as your landmark
cards.subtitle: North Harrison Street corridor · 301 N. Harrison St.
cards.notes: Head north on Harrison Street and use the center’s two-acre landscaped courtyard as a clear gathering point before browsing its directory.
cards.short_summary: An open-air center organized around a two-acre landscaped courtyard.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton Shopping Center is at 301 North Harrison Street and includes more than 40 storefronts and a two-acre landscaped courtyard.
cards.access_notes: Individual businesses set their own hours and purchase requirements.

cards.title: Read Princeton’s historical markers
cards.subtitle: Greenview Avenue corridor · 29 Greenview Ave.
cards.notes: Approach along Greenview Avenue and use the cemetery’s historic setting for a quiet, respectful walk; treat it as an active burial ground.
cards.short_summary: A historic cemetery associated with national political and scientific figures.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton Cemetery at 29 Greenview Avenue contains graves of a U.S. president, a vice president, and several Nobel laureates.
cards.access_notes: Be respectful of burial sites and posted cemetery rules.

cards.title: See Einstein’s former residence from the street
cards.subtitle: Mercer Street corridor · 112 Mercer St.
cards.notes: Walk Mercer Street for a streetside view of the house where Einstein lived from 1935 to 1955; it remains a private home.
cards.short_summary: Einstein’s longtime Princeton residence, viewable only from the public street.
cards.evidence_claim: Albert Einstein lived at 112 Mercer Street from 1935 to 1955; the residence is private and can be viewed from the street.
cards.source_title: Princeton: A Visitor’s Guide | Princeton Public Library
cards.access_notes: Private residence; view only from the public street and do not enter the property.
